summary: This excerpt from the novel's Book 4, part 26, follows Felix, Van and Rosa over wine as they resolve to rebuild a fragile community after some kind of collapse, with Felix insisting that failure is better than giving up. The narrative then skips years ahead, showing repeated cycles of rebuilding and breakup, Felix's hard physical work, and his eventual job keeping a small government's data-center running with Van. The tone mixes hope with ongoing hardship and loss.
one_line: Felix, Van and Rosa toast to rebuilding after collapse, then the story jumps years ahead to Felix's hard, uneven life running a small government's data-center.
key_facts: Felix says, "We're going to take this patch of the world where people are talking to each other, and we're going to expand it."
Felix says, "We'll probably fuck it up. We'll probably fail. I'd rather fail than give up, though."
Van tells Felix he is "crazier than Sario."
Felix says, "The world doesn't end. Humans aren't the kind of things that have endings."
Van says Felix "prefers Prime Minister" in a stagey whisper.
Rosa agrees to help on the condition that she is never asked to call Felix Prime Minister and he never calls her Minister of Health.
The three toast "To rebuilding," "To anything," and "To everything."
The group starts to rebuild the next day, then starts over after disagreements split them months later, again a year after that, and again five years later.
Felix digs ditches, salvages cans, buries the dead, plants and harvests, fixes cars, and learns to make biodiesel.
Felix eventually works in a data-center for a little government that wanted to keep records, and Van goes with him.
Old friends from the Distributed Republic of Cyberspace in chat rooms insist on calling Felix PM.
Felix's wounds never heal, and neither do most other people's, with lingering and sudden sicknesses and tragedy on tragedy.
Felix likes the data-center, where he never feels like it is the first or last days of a nation.
Van's skin fades from angry red to fine pink after anti-histamines.
